description: Six-session supervisor-led 1:1 certification track for leaders in training. Manager-facing discussion guide and sign-off gate for each session.

sessions.title: The Foundation of Leadership
sessions.purpose: Verify the employee is shifting their mindset from 'I am the boss' to 'I am building influence.'
sessions.coreConcept: Leadership is a verb (a process of influence), not a noun (a title). A leader's effectiveness is limited by their 'Lid' — their leadership skill. If their leadership is a 4, the team's results will never consistently hit a 5.
sessions.supervisorTip: In this first session, you are setting the tone for the entire certification. Be a 'Tour Guide' (Level 3), not a 'Travel Agent.' Show them you are also working on raising your own Lid.

blocks.title: The Case Study (Chris)
blocks.context: The trainee read about Chris, a top performer who plateaued after being promoted.
blocks.whatToLookFor: Does the trainee recognize that Chris is trying to 'work' his way out of a 'leadership' problem?

prompts.text: Why do you think high performers like Chris often struggle to move past Level 1 (Position)?

blocks.title: The Influence Inventory (The "Move")
blocks.context: The trainee identified a relationship where they only have 'Level 1' (Positional) influence and created a plan to build trust.
blocks.whatToLookFor: Is their plan specific? (e.g., "I'm going to ask for their feedback on X" vs. "I'll be nicer").

prompts.text: If their plan is too vague, ask: "How will that specific action change how that person views your leadership next week?"
Briefly share a time you relied too much on your title and what happened.

blocks.title: The Growth Commitment
blocks.context: The trainee identified a personal 'Lid' (a skill or habit) they want to raise.
blocks.whatToLookFor: Honesty. They should identify a genuine growth area (e.g., communication, emotional intelligence, delegation).

prompts.text: Offer one resource or 'look-out' to help them. "I love that goal. I'll keep an eye out for opportunities for you to practice that in our next team meeting."

sessions.gateLabel: Do not clear them for Module 2 unless:
successCriteria: They can explain the "Law of the Lid" in their own words.
They have a specific, actionable plan to move a Level 1 relationship toward Level 2.
They acknowledge that their title is just the starting point, not the finish line.
sessions.nextStep: Once you are satisfied with their reflection, direct them to begin Module 2: Level 1 - Position.

sessions.title: Level 1 – Position
sessions.purpose: Ensure the trainee understands that their title is a 'seat at the table,' not the power behind the engine.
sessions.coreConcept: Level 1 is based on Rights. It is the entry level where people follow because they have to.

blocks.title: The Case Study (Jordan)
blocks.whatToLookFor: Does the trainee see that Jordan's 'manual-first' approach is actually a 'position' problem?

prompts.text: In our day-to-day work, when is it most tempting to rely on 'because I said so' rather than explaining the 'why'?
If their "Relational Value" is just "being nice," challenge them. Ask: "How will you handle respect when a team member disagrees with you?"

blocks.title: Moving Toward People
blocks.whatToLookFor: A willingness to leave the 'comfort zone' of the job description.

prompts.text: Tell them about the first time you realized your title didn't mean people were actually following you.

sessions.gateLabel: Clear them for Module 3 if they:
successCriteria: Can identify the difference between a "Positional" mindset and a "Permissional" leadership.
Agree that "Leadership is action, not position".
Have committed to three core values that will drive their behavior.
sessions.nextStep: Direct them to begin Module 3: Level 2 - Permission.

sessions.sourceFile: HSPL Lesson 3, Level 2 - Supervisor Discussion Guide.pdf
sessions.title: Level 2 – Permission
sessions.purpose: Ensure the trainee isn't just 'being a friend,' but is building the relational capital required to lead people through difficult challenges.
sessions.coreConcept: Level 2 is based on Relationships. It is the level where the environment becomes pleasant, communication opens up, and trust is nurtured.

blocks.title: The Case Study (Taylor)
blocks.whatToLookFor: Does the trainee see that Taylor is actually stunting the team's growth by avoiding candor?

prompts.text: Why do high-producers get frustrated when a leader is 'too soft' and avoids performance conversations?

blocks.title: Relationship Audit
blocks.whatToLookFor: Look at the trainee's answers to the four questions. Are they surface-level or deep?

prompts.text: Ask: "How does knowing these non-business details help you lead this person differently?"
Tell them about a time you had to deliver a 'hard truth' to someone you cared about and how it ultimately helped the relationship or the team.

sessions.gateLabel: Clear them for Module 4 if they:
successCriteria: Understand that Level 2 is about permission, not just popularity.
Have a plan to deepen their knowledge of their team members as "whole people".
sessions.nextStep: Direct them to begin Module 4: Level 3 - Production.

sessions.title: Level 3 – Production
sessions.purpose: Move the trainee from individual contributor to leader of results.
sessions.coreConcept: Level 3 is based on Results. Leaders gain credibility and influence not just by being 'liked,' but because of what they have done for the organization.

blocks.title: The Case Study (Morgan)
blocks.context: Morgan is acting as a Travel Agent (sending people where they've never been) rather than a Tour Guide (taking people where they have personally gone).
blocks.whatToLookFor: Does the trainee recognize that Morgan is falling into the 'individual contributor' trap?

prompts.text: Morgan says doing it themselves is 'faster.' How does that mentality actually limit the team's results over the long term?

blocks.title: The Pareto Principle (80/20 Rule)
blocks.whatToLookFor: Look at the trainee's Responsibilities chart. Are their 'High Return' activities leadership-focused, or are they still clinging to technical tasks?

prompts.text: If they struggle to identify what to delegate, ask: "Which of your lower-ranked tasks would provide the best growth opportunity for one of your peers if you taught it to them?"

blocks.title: Small Victories & Momentum
blocks.whatToLookFor: A specific plan to build Momentum — the 'Great Exaggerator' that makes solving problems easier.

prompts.text: Tell them about a time when team momentum made a difficult goal feel easy, or when a lack of momentum made a small problem feel impossible.

sessions.gateLabel: Clear them for Module 5 if they:
successCriteria: Can explain the difference between a "Tour Guide" and a "Travel Agent".
Have identified their top 20% "High Return" activities.
Have a specific "small victory" plan to start building momentum this week.
sessions.nextStep: Direct them to begin Module 5: Level 4 - People Development.

sessions.title: Level 4 – People Development
sessions.purpose: Shift the trainee's focus from personal productivity to recruiting, positioning, and equipping others to lead.
sessions.coreConcept: Level 4 is based on Reproduction. The leader's focus shifts from personal productivity to recruiting, positioning, and equipping others to lead.

blocks.title: The Case Study (Parker)
blocks.whatToLookFor: Does the trainee see that Parker's 'indispensability' is actually a career bottleneck?

prompts.text: Why is it often harder for a top producer (Level 3) to shift into a developer (Level 4) mindset?

blocks.title: The 5-Step Equipping Process
blocks.whatToLookFor: Verify they have chosen a specific technical skill and a specific peer to mentor. The goal is to move from Step 1 (I do it) to Step 2 (I do it and you are with me).

prompts.text: If they chose a peer based solely on "Chemistry," challenge them to evaluate that person's Capacity (horsepower/ability) and Character (reliability).

blocks.title: The "Four Cs" Personal Plan
blocks.whatToLookFor: Maturity in identifying their own growth area.

prompts.text: Tell them about the first person you successfully 'reproduced' your skills in and how that allowed you to 'lead larger'.

sessions.gateLabel: Clear them for Module 6 if they:
successCriteria: Can define the "80/20" shift (80% focus on developing others).
Have a specific plan to initiate the 5-Step Equipping process with a peer.
Have committed to improving one of their own "Four Cs".
sessions.nextStep: Direct them to begin Module 6: Level 5 - The Pinnacle.

sessions.title: Level 5 – The Pinnacle
sessions.purpose: Confirm the trainee is building influence on who they are and what they represent, creating a legacy that outlasts them.
sessions.coreConcept: Level 5 is based on Respect. It is the highest level where influence is built on who the leader is and what they represent, creating a legacy that outlasts them.

blocks.title: The Case Study (Avery)
blocks.whatToLookFor: Does the trainee see that Avery's greatest success was the 'pipeline of leaders' left behind, not the projects Avery completed?

prompts.text: In our company, what specific character traits do we respect most in a leader who 'transcends' their job title?

blocks.title: Legacy Vision (The DNA)
blocks.whatToLookFor: Depth of character. Is their 'Legacy DNA' focused on personal advancement or on adding value to others and the organization?

prompts.text: If their vision is purely professional, ask: "Maxwell says you hire a 'whole person'. How does who you are outside of work impact your legacy at work?"

blocks.title: Crucible Moments
blocks.whatToLookFor: A willingness to be vulnerable. Level 5 leaders use their 'fumbles and flops' as teaching tools for others.

prompts.text: Share one of your own 'crucible moments' — a difficult experience that fundamentally changed your leadership perspective.

successCriteria: Can distinguish between Success (personal) and Significance (impact on others).
Have shared a clear "Legacy Vision" for their current role.
Commit to using a personal "crucible story" to mentor a peer this month.
sessions.nextStep: Award the How Successful People Lead Certification.
